issues.summary: Silent money DOUBLE-COUNT on a partial supplier rename — the case the rename detector exists for, and the case it cannot see. The alert fires only when the prior holder's supplierKey is ABSENT from this pull (orderapp.gs:854: `!pullSupplierKeys[priorHolders[ph].supplierKey]`). Renaming the free-text supplier cell on ONE invoice while other invoices in the 3-month window still carry the old spelling keeps the old key in pullSupplierKeys, so the guard evaluates false and nothing is raised. Verified empirically by running greenBeanPull_impl_ under the test mocks: sheet pre-seeded with greenbean rows 'acme/INV-700' ($500) and 'acme/INV-701' ($100); pull returns INV-700 under supplierKey 'acme coffee co' and INV-701 still under 'acme'. Result — Suppliers ends with THREE rows ['acme/INV-700' $500, 'acme/INV-701' $100, 'acme coffee co/INV-700' $500], greenbean total $1100 against a truth of $600, and calendarEvents is EMPTY (no greenbean_rename alert). The affected week IS resummarized, so the inflated figure is actively written into Summary and served by doGet. The control case (full rename, old key absent) does alert correctly, so the detector works — it just has no coverage of the more likely drift, since fixing the spelling on the invoice you happen to be looking at is exactly how a hand-typed sheet renames a supplier. docs/schema.md:61-65 states the detection unconditionally ('greenBeanPull detects the pattern and raises a greenbean_rename data-quality alert'), so the doc promises coverage that does not exist. Fix: replace the supplier-absence heuristic with the complete signal already available — any greenbean snapshot row whose storedDate falls inside greenBeanWindow_ but whose ref is absent from THIS pull's invoice set is an orphan (rename, deletion, or date-move), because the pull re-fetches the whole window by definition. That catches the partial rename, keeps the window bound round 7 added, and needs no supplier-presence guess.

A date correction upstream never propagates and is never flagged — the money stays attributed to the wrong ISO week permanently. The affected-week diff only reacts to a NEW ref (orderapp.gs:848) or a CHANGED total (orderapp.gs:863); an invoice whose ref and total are unchanged but whose dateLocal moved hits the snapshot, compares equal, and falls through with no addAffectedWeek and no alert. upsertRows_ never rewrites the date column (Code.gs:595-598 touch only amountCol and stampCol), so the stale date also survives the ingest. Verified empirically: Suppliers pre-seeded with 'acme/INV-800' $250 dated 2026-07-06, pull returns the same ref and total dated 2026-06-15 — the sheet still reads 2026-07-06, weeksResummarized 0, weeksQueued 0, calendarEvents empty. Two weeks are now wrong at once (the true week understated, the stale week overstated) and nothing distinguishes them from correct data, since both the ref and the total reconcile. Unlike the deletion and rename cases, this one is not in docs/schema.md's runbook at all, so an operator has neither a signal nor a documented procedure. The detection is one comparison inside the existing snapshot-hit branch (`snap.storedDate !== invoice.date`), and the remediation is the same runbook already written for deletions.

The abort-path data-quality alert shares its suppression key with the success path, so the more severe condition is silenced by the milder one. Both orderapp.gs:724 (ABORTED mid-fetch) and orderapp.gs:738 (successful pull with warnings) address source `GREENBEAN_SOURCE + '_upstream'` and derive the signature from the same hashed warning text, so they write and read the same ORDERAPP_DQ_SIG_greenbean_upstream property. A run that alerts on warning set W while succeeding, followed by a run that collects the same W and then ABORTS on a size guard or paging shortfall, computes an identical signature and is suppressed — the operator never sees the 'greenBeanPull ABORTED' message even though the whole window failed to ingest that week. The abort is still eventually caught by the fail-open counter, but only at the start of the NEXT weekly run (threshold 2), i.e. up to 7 days later. Give the abort path its own source suffix (e.g. '_upstream_abort') so the two conditions cannot suppress each other.

The rename suppression signature is stored raw while its two siblings hash, contradicting the rationale round 7 introduced. orderapp.gs:876 passes `'rename:' + suspectedRenames.slice().sort().join('|')` — the full concatenated text of every suspected rename, each entry roughly 60 characters — whereas the upstream-warning signature (orderapp.gs:744) and the flags signature (orderapp.gs:771) are hashed/compacted. Apps Script caps a single Script Property value at 9KB, so a large rename batch makes setProperty throw; the throw is swallowed by orderAppRaiseDataQualityAlert_'s catch (orderapp.gs:216), which means the signature is never persisted and the identical alert re-fires every weekly run. orderAppSignatureHash_ already exists and is applied two lines away; use it here too.

A BLANK_SUPPLIER intake row lands in Suppliers under the literal supplier name 'greenbean'. greenBeanInvoices_ emits `supplier: group.supplierRaw` (orderapp.gs:491), and when supplierRaw is empty canonicalSupplier_ (Code.gs:353-356) falls through `row.supplier` to `SUPPLIER_NAMES['greenbean'] || 'greenbean'` — SUPPLIER_NAMES has no greenbean entry, so the source token becomes the supplier name. That row then surfaces in Summary as a line item called 'greenbean' sitting beside real supplier names, while its invoice_ref reads 'unknown/<num>' (the producer's supplierKey fallback) — two different placeholder spellings for the same row. The underlying data problem does raise the flags alert, so this is presentation rather than money, but a single explicit fallback (e.g. 'Green Bean — unnamed supplier') would keep the two columns consistent and make the row self-describing in the weekly report.

A resummarize backlog beyond GREENBEAN_RESUM_CAP is invisible on a scheduled run. greenBeanPull_impl_ summarizes at most 5 weeks per run (orderapp.gs:509, :894) and returns the shortfall as `weeksQueued` (orderapp.gs:939) — but a trigger-invoked run has no reader for that return value, and unlike every other noteworthy state in this file the overflow gets no Logger.log and no alert. A backfill or a bulk edit that touches the whole 3-month window queues ~13 weeks, so Summary stays stale for the undrained ones for up to two further weekly runs with nothing said. TODO.md's bring-up runbook mitigates the first-pull case by having Jake summarize the window manually, but not the steady-state case. One log line when remainingQueue is non-empty would close it.
